Rakhi Das vs B.M.T.C on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126814218/
1

This petition is filed by the LR's of one deceased Kum.Taneha Kumari D/o Sri. Rakhi Das, under Section 166 of M.V. Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- in respect of her death in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 26.02.2025 at about 6- 45 am when Taneha Kumari was proceeding as a pedestrian on Hosur Main road, Beritena Agrahara, Bengaluru city, when she crossing the road Opposite to Shayi Garments, at that time, driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.No.KA-57/F-0838 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed from Hosa road junction towards Konappana Agrahara junction and dashed Taneha Kumari and caused the accident.
Due to which she sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
Thereafter, Postmortem was conducted in St. John's Hospital and dead body was handed over to her family members.
Petitioners have more than Rs.1,00,000/- for transportation of dead body, last rituals and funeral expenses.
3. At the time of accident deceased was hale and healthy she was aged about 19 years and she was working as Helper at Shayi garments and was earning Rs.21,000/- p.m.
That deceased was the only earning member in the family due to her untimely death petitioners are put to great financial hardship.
The accident is due to rash and negligent driving of driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.No.KA-57/F-0838.

The Electronic (SCCH-12) 3 MVC No.2339/2025 City Traffic police have registered a case against the said driver in Crime No.21/2025 against him for the offence P/U/S,
281, 106(1), 125(b) of BNS.
The respondent being Owner-cum- Insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.
In the written statement the Respondent contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent admits the ownership of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.No.KA-57/F-0838 and denied the entire averments made in the petition.
It is contended that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus.

Further, it has denied the age, occupation and income of deceased and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased and also denied the expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.
On all these grounds respondent prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this court has framed following;
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LR's of one Taneha Kumari and competent persons to file this petition?

Whether petitioners prove that on 26.02.2025 at about 6.45 AM, Taneha Kumari was pedestrian on left side of Hosur Main Road, by observing traffic rules and crossing the said road opposite to Rakhi Das vs B.M.T.C on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126814218/
2

Shahi Garments, driver of one BMTC but bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0838 driven the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed to Taneha Kumarui and caused accident, due to which she sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
6. To prove their case, petitioner no.1 entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.12 documents are marked.
On the contrary, driver of the respondent Corporation got examined as RW.1 and through him Ex.R1 and 2 are marked.
7. Heard learned counsel for both sides.
Perused records.

8. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per final order,
 for the following,
 (SCCH-12) 5 MVC No.2339/2025  REASONS 9. ISSUE No.1 :
Petitioners
, to prove that they are LR's of Taneha Kumari, 1st petitioner got examined as P.W.1.
In his affidavit he has stated that he is father of deceased and 2 nd petitioner is mother of the deceased.
In support of the same he has produced aadhar cards of petitioners and deceased, at Ex.P10 to 12.
They show deceased is the daughter of petitioners herein.
Respondent has not seriously disputed the relationship with the deceased.

Therefore on the basis of Aadhaar cards and the oral evidence of P.W.1 this court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are the LR's of Taneha Kumari and competent persons to file this petition.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE No.2:

According to petitioners driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.No.KA-57/F-0838,
was negligent.
To prove the same, P.W.1 in his chief examination affidavit stated about the negligence of bus driver.

He relied upon the police documents i.e., FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar,
Vehicle seizure mahazar, Charge sheet, IMV report, PM report, Inquest report and Statement of witnesses and in that regard.

Rakhi Das vs B.M.T.C on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126814218/
3 11.
On perusal of those documents it can be seen that, brother of the deceased / son of 1st petitioner Sri.Ashish Kumar, is first informant and he is not an eye witness to the incident.
On the same day of the accident, FIR is registered at 10.00 am.

In the spot panchanama it can be seen that it is Hosur Main road, where there is metro pillar,
there is no obstruction in the road, and accident took place in the middle of the road.
As per the IMV report, front windscreen glass broken and radiator grill damaged.
As per postmortem report, death is due to hemorrhagic shock due to multiple injuries sustained.
After investigation charge sheet is filed against bus driver but he has not challenged the same before any competent forum.
13. On the contrary, to prove the negligence on part of the deceased in the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle got examined as RW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief.

He has reiterated the contention taken in the written statement and got marked two documents i.e one CD and one complaint given by him to joint Commissioner of police (Traffic) on 26.02.2025 and received by the police on 28.02.2025.
In the complaint he has mentioned that he was not negligent in the accident.
He has produced one CD said to be containing video of the accident.
According to him the said video is taken from the camera when the offending bus was moving and the camera was fixed inside the BMTC BUS.
The same is produced by the bus driver.
The same is not accompanied by Sec. 63 BSA certificate.
He has not mentioned about the said video in his complaint at Ex. R2.
The same is not mentioned by the police in final report also.
Therefore, the video recording is not admissible in evidence in the absence of Sec. 63 BSA certificate.
However, it is necessary to observe that time of accident is 6.45 AM.
Deceased could have examined the moving vehicles on the road.
There was no Zeebra crossing, and there was cement road dividers on both sides.
Therefore, pedestrians were not supposed to cross the road at that spot.
RW.1 bus driver is not only accused but he is also eye witness to the incident.
He has stated in his complaint as well as in evidence that deceased suddenly rushed to the road and he was on the left side of the road.
He has given the complaint to the police on the same day of the accident.
Hence there is equal contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident and the quantum of negligence of bus driver and decesed is 50% each.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above reasons, petitioners are entitled for compensation for the negligence of bus driver.
Respondent disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
To prove the age of the deceased petitioners mentioned in the petition that deceased was aged 19 years at the time of accident.
They have produced Notarized Copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P.12.
It shows she was born on 28-03-2005.
As on the date of accident deceased was aged 19 years 10 months 29 days.
Therefore it is considered that the deceased was aged about 19 years at the time of accident.

Rakhi Das vs B.M.T.C on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126814218/
4 16.
In the petition it is mentioned that deceased was working as a Helper in Shayi Garments and earning Rs.21,000/- p.m.
To prove her occupation and income no document is produced.
Hence, notional income has to be considered.
Accident having taken place in 2025, the notional income of deceased is considered as Rs.17,000/- per month and the quantum of compensation is determined as under:
17. Loss of dependency :
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of self employed 40% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group below 40 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 19 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, in the present case the monthly income of deceased is Rs.17,000/- +
6,800/- = Rs.23,800/-.
Further deceased being unmarried  (half) of her income shall be deducted towards her personal expenses.

Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as under;
Rs. 11,900 X 12 months = Rs. 1,42,800/-
Rs.1,42,800/- X 18 multiplier to the age group of 18-25 years = Rs. 25,70,400/-
As such

, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.
25,70,400/-
18.
Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being LR's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their daughter due to her death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the (SCCH-12) 9 MVC No.2339/2025 opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs. 50,000 /- is awarded.
19. Loss of filial Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident being taken place in the year 2025, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,150/-, for funeral expenses Rs.18,150/- and for loss of consortium Rs. 48,400/- the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:

No.
1. Loss of Dependency : 25,70,400/-
2. Loss of love & affection : 50,000/-
3. Loss of Consortium to : 96,800/-
 petitioner No. 1 and 2  ( Rs.48,400/- each)
4. Loss of estate : 18,150-00 Rakhi Das vs B.M.T.C on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126814218/
5 5.
Funeral expenses : 18,150-00

Contributory negligence on (-)13,76,750/-
 part of the deceased at@50%
 Grand Total Rs.13,76,750/-
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs. 13,76,750/- from the hands of 1st (SCCH-12) 10 MVC No.2339/2025 respondent insurance company.
Hence, I answer this Issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
20. ISSUE No.4:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- in respect of death of Taneha Kumri in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
They being LR's of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 40:60.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs. 13,76,750/-/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.

In view of Respondent being Owner-cum- internal Insurer of offending vehicle is hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 2 months from the date of this order.

Out of the total compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioners, (SCCH-12)
11 MVC No.2339/2025 they are entitled to the compensation in the apportionment of 40:60.
In such apportionment entire compensation awarded to petitioners shall be released in their favour without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
